posts.body_html:
The Great Move: sounds like a title to a movie that's Rated R, doesn't it? Well, with all the cursing, it's a good thing that this wasn't filmed, haha! Anyhow, as many of you know, my entire collection had to be moved from the old site where it had been for more than a decade! I've moved 7 times in my life, and this was the most painful one EVER! Some of you are probably wondering why Mike Wang wasn't himself for the past few weeks....well, now you'll see why!

I work 6.5 days of the week, have a new baby, and then had to deal with this! Needless to say, I had to hire a crew to do most of this (and I'm thankful that we were able to save enough in advance for the move!), and it was a Nightmare on Elm Street (rated R for sure)! There won't be any venting here, just imagine a very stressful situation, and then the movers trying to double the estimated price on you the very last minute without any warning or notice. It was a great learning experience, that's for sure.

To their credit, they did a great job, just not double the estimate type of work! It took 5 people 6 days to complete everything!!! Below is an over-simplified photo-journal of the whole thing:


the last photo of the collection at the old grow site, this spot will be missed:





All GONE! Gosh, this spot looks like a ghost town with no plants!


New site to the left, and old tubs to the right. I was amazed that the crew was able to carry every last pool by placing a sheet under neath them and lifting it up with 4 people per tub. Even the pools that were as fragile as thin ice were transferred this way:



Yes, it was impossibly hard to water these as they temporarily sat on this slope:



Not the best set up, but it's supposed to be temporary...I'm going to have to move again in the near future if you can believe that! beds were built, with some soft woodchips underneath. They came in with a mini-bull dozer and leveled out this spot within half a day, it was pretty amazing. However, to do fine adjustments and build the wooden support walls was complicated and took a while. Everything that is potted went into this section, and everything that were in community trays went to the "overflow" spot (you'll see):


After days of hard work, here they are finally situated in the new spots. The beds are lined with plastic that probably won't last long. Thing is, the beds aren't very level, so watering is incredibly difficult. Some plants are over-watered, and others are wilting from being too dry....with the tubs, I could always level the gravel underneath, but I can't readjust the plastic since it's stapled in. Long story short, if you ever attempt something on this scale, each bed should be made up of multiple sections so if one section isn't level, the whole thing isn't affected:



What you can't tell from this photo is that many of the beds are only 1/4 occupied. There's significantly way more space here because it's being effciently used. round tubs wastes a lot of space in comparison, will never go back to them:





Here's the overflow spot. After the entire move was completed, I had plants all mixed and in complete chaos. This spot isn't level like the other, so with each community tray, I had to level the woodchips. Needless to say, it took many days to organize this. After looking at both spots together, I realized holy crap, there's soooo many plants:



Well, there it is! There's still a bunch to do:the potted plants keep falling over, and it takes a good 20 minutes every day to pick them up, so that's pretty frustrating. Having the beds unleveled is challenging and I'm still trying to figure out how to make this work. It's certainly a lot more work, I used to get away with watering every 2-3 days, but now, even on cool days, if it isn't watered 1-2x per day, I get plants wilting. Nightmares go away, and it'll all be figured out in time!

posts.body_html: Lemna never really affects anything, except that it will cover everything, which can be a pain sometimes.  Azolla does have a tendency to crash, but only because the duckweed usually chokes it out.  I've tried many times to get pure Azolla cultures started, but with frogs moving Lemna around, its almost impossible.  As far as how they effect other plants, I haven't noticed any difference at all.
